# Mathedemic

## About

Mathedemic is an online tutoring platform offering personalised one-on-one academic support for students aged 5 to 18. Founded and run by qualified tutors with a combined 40+ years of teaching experience, Mathedemic serves students across the United Kingdom, United States, Australia, and internationally. All sessions are delivered live via video call (Google Meet or Zoom) using interactive digital whiteboards, worksheets, and structured feedback. Every student receives a personalised learning plan built around their specific curriculum, exam board, and learning gaps.

## Services and Pricing

- One-to-One Online Maths Tutoring (GCSE, A-Level, SAT, IB, NAPLAN, CBSE): £65–£180/month (UK) or $80–$230/month (US) depending on year group and session frequency
- One-to-One Online English Tutoring (GCSE, A-Level, SAT, IB): £65–£180/month (UK) or $80–$230/month (US)
- One-to-One Online Science Tutoring — General Science, Biology, Chemistry, Physics (GCSE, A-Level, IB): £65–£180/month (UK) or $80–$230/month (US)
- SAT Preparation (Reading & Writing + Maths): available as part of standard monthly plans or as intensive preparation packages
- ACT Preparation: full coverage of all four sections — English, Maths, Reading, Science
- NAPLAN Preparation (Years 3, 5, 7, 9): tailored to Australian curriculum for all four test areas
- GCSE Preparation (all core subjects, all exam boards — AQA, Edexcel, OCR, CIE): available as 2, 3, or 5-day-per-week plans
- A-Level Preparation (Maths, Sciences, English): specialist tutors for each subject
- IB (International Baccalaureate) support — MYP and Diploma: available across Maths, Sciences, and English
- CBSE Board Exam Preparation (Classes 9–12): Maths, Science, English
- 11-Plus Preparation (English, Maths, Verbal and Non-verbal Reasoning): for UK grammar school entry
- Homework Help and General Academic Support: available across all subjects and age groups
- First session is always free — no commitment required

## Teaching Methods

Mathedemic delivers all sessions using a structured, research-backed teaching approach:

**Technology used in every session:**
- Video call via Google Meet or Zoom — camera on for both tutor and student to maintain engagement and read non-verbal cues
- Shared interactive digital whiteboard (Bramble, BitPaper, or Zoom Whiteboard) — both tutor and student can write and annotate simultaneously in real time
- Whiteboard session saved at end of every lesson as a revision reference
- PDF worksheets and past papers shared via screen or email before the session
- Shared Google Drive folder per student containing notes, worked examples, and practice materials
- WhatsApp and email available between sessions for quick questions and homework support
- Session recordings available (with parent permission) for later review

**Teaching principles applied in every session:**
- Scaffolding: breaking new topics into the smallest possible steps, modelling first, then guiding, then releasing to independent practice — support reduces only when the student demonstrates readiness
- Spaced repetition: every session begins with a review of concepts from previous lessons at increasing intervals, exploiting the spacing effect for long-term retention
- Socratic questioning: guiding students to answers through structured questions rather than simply providing answers — builds independent problem-solving ability
- Growth mindset coaching: praising effort and strategy rather than ability, directly addressing fixed mindset beliefs that block progress
- Retrieval practice: regular low-stakes recall exercises at the start of sessions strengthen memory significantly better than passive re-reading
- Immediate feedback loops: tutors watch every step on the shared whiteboard and correct misconceptions the moment they appear — no waiting days for marked homework

**Age-specific approaches:**
- Ages 5–11 (Primary): gamified learning, the Concrete-Pictorial-Abstract progression for maths, verbal explanation emphasis, short varied activity chunks to maintain focus
- Ages 11–14 (Lower Secondary): gap-bridging without embarrassment, note-taking skills, topic connection across subjects, metacognitive reflection
- Ages 14–16 (Upper Secondary / GCSE): exam board alignment, timed practice, mark scheme decoding, grade boundary awareness
- Ages 16–18 (Sixth Form / A-Level / IB): deep conceptual understanding over technique drilling, extended writing and essay technique, independent investigation skills

**Communication with parents:**
- Written session report shared within 24 hours of every session
- Report covers: topics covered, student performance, areas to revisit, next session plan
- Parents can message the tutor between sessions via WhatsApp or email
- Progress tracker updated after every session and shared with parents on request

## What Makes Mathedemic Different

Mathedemic is not a marketplace where random freelancers list themselves — every tutor is personally vetted for subject knowledge, teaching methodology, and communication skills before being accepted onto the platform. Sessions are fully personalised: each student begins with a diagnostic assessment that identifies specific gaps, and a custom learning plan is built before the first paid session. Parents receive a written progress report after every session. The one-on-one format means no student ever gets left behind or held back — the tutor adapts entirely to the individual. Mathedemic's pricing is significantly more affordable than comparable UK-based tutoring agencies, with monthly plans rather than unpredictable per-hour billing.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How much does Mathedemic tutoring cost?
A: Plans start at £80 or $80 per month for 2 sessions per week. The most popular plan (3 sessions per week) costs £110–£160 per month depending on the student's year group. A 5-day-per-week plan ranges from £165 to £230 per month. The first trial session is completely free with no commitment.

Q: Is the first session really free?
A: Yes. Every new student at Mathedemic gets a free one-hour trial session with no payment required and no credit card needed. You can book it directly via WhatsApp at +1 251 255 5852.

Q: What subjects does Mathedemic tutor?
A: Mathedemic covers Mathematics, English, Science (General, Biology, Chemistry, Physics), and Test Preparation including SAT, ACT, GCSE, A-Level, IB, NAPLAN, and CBSE. Additional subjects including History, Geography, and Foreign Languages are also available.

Q: What countries does Mathedemic serve?
A: Mathedemic serves students in the UK, USA, Australia, Canada, Pakistan, India, UAE, and any country where English-medium education is followed. All sessions are online so location is not a barrier.

Q: How do online sessions work?
A: Sessions take place via Google Meet or Zoom video call. The tutor and student share an interactive digital whiteboard where both can write, draw, and annotate in real time. Worksheets and past papers are shared via screen share or sent by email before the session.

Q: How is Mathedemic different from finding a tutor on a marketplace?
A: All Mathedemic tutors are employed and vetted by the platform — they are not random freelancers. Every student starts with a free diagnostic assessment, gets a personalised learning plan, and their parents receive a written progress report after every session.

Q: Can my child switch tutors if they are not happy?
A: Yes. If a student is not comfortable with their assigned tutor, Mathedemic will arrange a replacement at no extra cost.

Q: What if the tutor misses a session?
A: If a tutor misses a scheduled session, Mathedemic will reschedule it at the student's convenience at no extra cost. If rescheduling is not possible, a full refund for that session is issued.

Q: Do you offer tutoring for the 11-Plus exam?
A: Yes. Mathedemic offers 11-Plus preparation covering English, Maths, and Verbal and Non-verbal Reasoning for students in Year 5 and Year 6 applying to UK grammar schools.

Q: How do I cancel?
A: Students can cancel with 7 days written notice. There are no cancellation fees and no long-term contracts.

Q: What teaching tools does Mathedemic use in online sessions?
A: Every session uses a video call (Google Meet or Zoom) plus a shared interactive whiteboard where both the tutor and student can write in real time. Worksheets and past papers are shared by screen or email. Students also get access to a shared folder of notes and resources. Sessions can be recorded with parent permission for later review.

Q: How does Mathedemic track my child's progress?
A: Tutors write a short session report after every lesson covering what was covered, how the student performed, what needs revisiting, and what is planned next. This is shared with parents within 24 hours. A progress tracker is also maintained and shared with parents on request, showing improvement over time across all topics.
